articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations today targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These actions aim to disrupt financial networks supporting illicit drug trafficking and terrorist organizations globally.
Further details on the specific individuals and entities designated, and the implications of these designations, are available on the OFAC website.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces International Criminal Court Designation and Burma-related Designation Removal
body: OFAC has issued a new designation related to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and simultaneously announced the removal of a Burma-related designation.
This action also includes the issuance of General Licenses, which provide specific authorizations for certain transactions.
The details of the ICC designation and the reasons for the Burma-related removal are outlined in the official announcement.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-related General License

This license provides specific authorizations for certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under existing Russia sanctions programs.
Parties involved in Russia-related dealings should review the new General License for applicable permissions and conditions.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-related Designations and Amends Russia-related General License
body: OFAC has announced new designations targeting entities and individuals connected to Iran, alongside the issuance of a new Iran-related General License.
Concurrently, an existing Russia-related General License has been amended, indicating adjustments to authorized activities concerning Russia.
These actions reflect ongoing efforts to address Iranian proliferation activities and refine the scope of Russia sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes and Updates Designations, Publishes Iran-related Alert
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced several designation removals and updates, alongside the publication of a new Iran-related OFAC Alert.
The alert warns foreign financial institutions that they could be targeted without advance notification if they continue to transact with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions.
Additionally, an Iran-related Frequently Asked Question has been amended, providing further clarification on existing sanctions policy.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: OFAC has announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter terrorism activities.
These actions are part of ongoing efforts to disrupt the financial support networks of terrorist organizations worldwide.
The specific details of these designations are available on the Treasury Department's website.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-related Designations and Targets Transnational Criminal Organizations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has implemented new Iran-related designations and designation updates, alongside a new designation targeting Transnational Criminal Organizations.
These actions are part of Operation Economic Outcast, launched in August 2026, to cut off financial resources supporting the Iranian regime.
Additionally, an Iran-related Determination and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question have been published, providing further guidance on the scope of these sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Removes Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations

Concurrently, several designations related to Belarus, counter narcotics, and Libya have been removed.
These actions reflect a dynamic approach to sanctions, adding new targets while delisting others based on evolving circumstances.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Broad Designations Across Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-related, and Non-Proliferation Programs

These actions underscore the U.S. government's commitment to combating various threats to national security and foreign policy interests.
The comprehensive nature of these designations indicates a concerted effort to disrupt multiple illicit networks simultaneously.

articles.headline: OFAC Publishes Regulatory Amendments and New Cuba Sanctions Regulations

articles.headline: OCC Assesses $350 Million Civil Money Penalty Against American Express National Bank for BSA/AML Deficiencies
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has announced a cease-and-desist order and a $350 million civil money penalty against American Express National Bank for significant deficiencies in its Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program.
The OCC determined that the bank failed to establish and maintain a BSA/AML compliance program reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the BSA and its implementing regulations.

Deficiencies included inadequate resources, insufficient staff expertise, systemic internal control gaps, weak independent testing, and inadequate BSA/AML training, leading to a failure to timely identify and report approximately $13 billion of suspected trade-based money laundering activity over the past decade.
articles.source: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
